reasons: The candidate multiplies by a constant 100 that is not in the Datadog source; the hard rules forbid unsourced numeric constants, and no unit difference justifies it.
postgresql.backends (non-monotonic sum, unit 1, count of backends per database) is a reasonable match for postgresql.connections, so the quantity and unit are fine once the constant is removed.
Grouping by postgresql_database_name matches the Datadog by {db}, and that label is observed in the dataset.

Template variables $table (prefix table), $db (prefix db) and $host (prefix host) default to *, so they must become matchers such as postgresql_database_name=~"$db" and host_name=~"$host" (both observed). The candidate drops them, which changes the series set.
$scope has no prefix and default *, so dropping it is correct.
Fix: remove the 100 multiplier and add the prefixed template-variable matchers using the observed dataset labels.
